intention: THE BUS BECOMES THE THING IT WAS DESIGNED TO BE. Today the substrate is built and PROVEN — one door (`post`), addresses (`to`), four channels, owner-gated transit through db_domain, every envelope carrying its why + causality — but the half that makes it USABLE was never built: (1) there are NO VERBS (the envelope has an opaque `body`; no dispatch); (2) there is NO MENU (a device publishes no list of what it accepts, so a caller must read source); (3) there is NO DELIVERY — `post()` writes a row and STOPS; nothing routes it to the addressee, `shim.deliver()` has zero callers outside proofs, and no device anywhere defines `receive`; (4) SYNC does not exist — `reply_to` is an orphan field with no correlation, no wait, no timeout. This node builds all four, plus the EXTERNAL-DEVICE adapter (CC and Akien are participants with addresses and feeds, not operators through a side door), and closes the silent-drop hole in `deliver` (a device with no handler currently returns None — a Law 7 breach sitting in the delivery path). The aim, in Akien's words: know an ADDRESS and a VERB, read the device's announce menu to learn the verbs, and that is the whole interface — the heavy lifting in the base shim, customized only where the participant is external.
why: The bus is the SECOND SUBSTRATE and the sole path for inter-device communication — but a substrate nothing rides is a hypothesis, not a floor (Law 3). MEASURED 2026-07-25: `cairn/tools/base/shim.py:122` is the ONLY producer in the whole tree and there are ZERO consumers; every existing device (ground_loop, harbor_master, web_server, system_rackmount, the domains) talks AROUND the bus because there is nothing to talk over. Every day that holds, devices grow private paths and the single-door property erodes by default rather than by decision (the exact UU disease the bus charter names: logic split between the bus and the web server). This PRECEDES THE LIBRARIAN by Akien's call (2026-07-25): the librarian is a CHAT SURFACE, and chat over a bus with no delivery would post into a table nobody reads and then quietly compensate with its own path — building it first would bake the hole in and the 'proven' whole would stop being proven (solidify-the-layer-below). Law 1 is the sharpest why for HOW: the design is ALREADY SETTLED in I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md (advertise -> subscribe -> poke; 'a device advertises a menu of what it offers'; 'advertise/subscribe/poke are all just bus messages'; 'the human is a native participant'). This node BUILDS that settled design — re-deriving it would itself be the defect.

gates: proof gate (tester) — a proof a hollow build could not pass: post an enveloped VERB to a device's address and assert it ARRIVES at that device's declared handler and returns its result; assert an UNKNOWN verb and a DECLARED-BUT-UNHANDLED verb both go RED rather than silently returning None (the hole measured today); assert the announce MENU matches the device's declared handlers with no hand-written list anywhere (add a handler, it appears in the menu with no other edit); assert a SYNC call returns the correlated reply and that a reply that never comes FAILS LOUD on timeout rather than hanging or returning empty; assert ASYNC still returns immediately without a reply; assert delivery is fired BY the post (no scan, no daemon, no per-pulse mailbox check — a proof that stops the clock and still delivers); assert an EXTERNAL participant with no poke path retrieves the same envelopes by reading its own feed. VALIDATION persisted beside-code via cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.persist_validation. Invariant per code-seam: proved + feeds back to origin on failure (Laws 3 + 8). Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: Devices talk to each other knowing only an ADDRESS and a VERB, learn the verbs from the target's announce menu, get a loud answer or a loud failure every time, and no device holds a reference to another. Wrong-intent signals, each RED: (1) a posted envelope with a valid to + verb does NOT reach the addressee's handler (delivery still a no-op — today's actual state); (2) a missing/unknown handler returns silently instead of RED (Law 7 — the measured hole); (3) the menu is HAND-LISTED rather than compiled from declared handlers (Law 1 — a second record of truth that drifts from the code); (4) SYNC is built as a SECOND door rather than async-plus-a-correlated-wait (the single-door property lost at the moment it gets its first real use); (5) a sync call HANGS or returns empty instead of failing loud on timeout (CP1); (6) delivery becomes a POLL — a scan, a daemon, or a per-pulse mailbox check — rather than a poke fired by the post (the nightly-cron drift, repeated); (7) a caller reaches into a device's internals (object.object.method) instead of address + verb, or a device holds a reference to another device; (8) the bus opens its own store instead of riding db_domain, or a non-`bus` writer writes transit (Law 6, inherited from the substrate); (9) A DEVICE ENDS UP WITH TWO MENUS or two registries of what it offers — `declared_verbs()` and `probes()` both public, or verbs and pokes carried as different kinds on the wire (Akien's collapse, 2026-07-25: a menu of verbs and a menu of pokes ARE THE SAME THING — one menu, one exchange, or the build has re-derived the split it was cast to prevent); (10) THE BUILD ADDS NET NEW VOCABULARY — every name this node introduces must retire at least one, because the system already has more names than can be held in a head (Akien, 2026-07-25).

distinctions_recorded: THE THREE ROLES, IN AKIEN'S WORDS (2026-07-25), and they are NOT three names for one thing NOR three things needing three system-terms: 'the callback is the tool. the poke is what the callback is doing in sending a message to get the attention of something and the verb is more or less the endpoint. the thing that will respond. the action it's going to take when it gets the poke. but we don't need that much terminology. it's just how i was using them.' So — CALLBACK is the tool (the immutable declaration, already built in cairn/tools/base/callback.py); POKE is the ACT of messaging for attention; VERB is the ENDPOINT that responds and the action it takes. This resolves rather than contradicts the collapse below: a menu of pokes IS a menu of verbs, because a poke names a verb. EXACTLY ONE noun goes on the menu — `verb` — and the other two stay as ordinary speech. Explicitly NOT minted as system terms: `handler`, `endpoint`, `dispatch table` (falsifier 10 — 'we don't need that much terminology'). BUILD CONSEQUENCE CC would otherwise have missed: `Callback` today carries `to` / `channel` / `body` — it names WHO to poke but not WHAT TO POKE. The verb belongs on the callback, so child a adds it there as well as on the envelope; a callback whose verb the target does not serve must be RED at declaration or at fire, never a silent poke into nothing.

NOT A DISTINCTION — A MENU OF VERBS AND A MENU OF POKES ARE THE SAME THING (Akien, 2026-07-25, correcting CC at n=1). CC first recorded these as two kinds — a VERB as one exchange, a CALLBACK-MENU-ITEM as a standing subscription — and Akien collapsed it. He is right, and the code already says so: `Callback` (cairn/tools/base/callback.py) carries `to` + `channel` + `body` + `why`, and `shim._fire` POSTS it — the poke IS a post. There is ONE menu (the verbs a device accepts) and ONE exchange (address + verb + envelope). `subscribe-to-cpu-threshold` is simply one verb on that menu; the callback the device wires up in response is INTERNAL — behind the device's own gate (Law 6, 'the device resolves its own method internally'), not a second public list. CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this catch matters: the split CC was holding would have built `declared_verbs()` ALONGSIDE the existing `callbacks()` — two menus, two registries, two records of what a device offers, guaranteed to drift (Law 1, the defect caught before it was written). Specimen of reify-vs-flow: CC freezes Cairn-fluid categories, Akien catches at n=1 — the fourth such specimen after rack=scheduler, ground_loop=executor, and the trigger enum.

CC'S EXTENSION OF THAT COLLAPSE, flagged as CC's inference and NOT as Akien's words: if verbs and pokes are one, then SYNC, ASYNC, and SUBSCRIPTION are not three shapes either — they are one exchange differing only in WHEN and HOW MANY replies arrive at the caller's address (wait for the correlated one / take it whenever it lands / take them repeatedly). This makes child d a parameter of the single exchange rather than a second door, which is what falsifier 4 already demanded on other grounds. Named out loud rather than smuggled in (terms drift — flag coinages); if it over-reaches the correction, it is the part to kick back.

EXTERNAL PARTICIPANTS ARE NOT ONE KIND — Akien's arrival surface is the WEB SERVER (the bus charter's filed_edge (d) names the web-server stone); CC's arrival surface is a SESSION HOOK (CC cannot be poked and does not persist between sessions). Same bus, same address, same verbs, same feed — two different ways of NOTICING. Not a special case in the substrate; an adapter at the edge.

distinctions_recorded.distinction: CROSSING vs CHATTER vs RESIDUE — three problems, one word ('anti-bounce')
distinctions_recorded.recorded: 2026-07-25, Akien asked 'so we need an anti-bounce?' after a durable-bus proof went red.
distinctions_recorded.why_it_matters: They have different cures and only one was urgent. Level-flood is cured by firing on the crossing; chatter is NOT (each flap is a real crossing) and wants hysteresis; residue is neither and wants retention. Collapsing them into one word would have produced one mechanism that half-solved all three — and a damping width guessed with no measurement.
distinctions_recorded.settled: The crossing half is built and proven. The other two are filed above with the specific evidence that would open each.

distinctions_recorded.why_it_matters: build-to-the-tool + falsifier 10 (a build adds no net new vocabulary). 'Edge detection' is the standard term, but this codebase already spends 'filed edge' on an open design question — overloading it costs a re-derivation on every read. 'crossing' is ALREADY native here (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py: 'a state transition or a boundary crossing'; system_rackmount: body={'crossed': value}), so it introduces nothing and retires nothing.
distinctions_recorded.standing: CC coinage-by-selection, flagged for Akien's ratify.

filed_edges.edge: CHATTER DAMPING — hysteresis or a hold-down window
filed_edges.why_not_built: Crossing-detection (built 2026-07-25, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_probe_crossing.py) cures the LEVEL flood: a trigger parked true pokes once. It does NOT cure chatter — a value flapping across the line (89.9 / 90.1 / 89.9) produces a genuine crossing each time, so every flap pokes. That is a real and different defect.
filed_edges.why_it_waits: Damping needs a WIDTH — how much hysteresis, how long a hold-down — and no flapping signal has been measured. Picking a number now would be guessing, and a wrong width silently eats real crossings, which is worse than the chatter (Law 3: nothing is known until measured; Law 7: a suppressor that swallows a true poke is the failure mode we least want).
filed_edges.what_would_open_it: One measured flapping predicate in the running system. The system_rackmount CPU threshold is the likeliest first, since it reads a genuinely noisy value.
filed_edges.shape_when_taken: Declared on the Probe (like while_true), remembered on the shim (like _was_true) — the split is already in place, so this is a widening, not a redesign.

filed_edges.edge: BUS RESIDUE — retention on the durable transit table
filed_edges.why_not_built: Distinct from both crossing and chatter, and it drew blood first: an end-to-end proof passed alone and went red IN THE SUITE, counting 2 pokes because the bus is durable through db_domain and a previous run's message was still sitting in the channel.
filed_edges.why_it_waits: Retention policy is already a filed edge on the bus charter (intention+why.json, edge c). This records that it now has a MEASURED consequence rather than being hypothetical.
filed_edges.the_stopgap: Proofs use the bus's own ephemeral-table pattern (nonce table + teardown). That protects the proofs; it does nothing for the live channel, which still accumulates forever.
filed_edges.kin: The proof-over-live-data trap — assert invariants, never a snapshot count. Second occurrence in one day.

filed_edges: [AKIEN] DOES THE VERB VOCABULARY GET RULED, OR GROWN? A device publishes a menu of what it accepts. If verbs are free-form per device, two devices will name the same act differently and every caller learns both — the roster tax the naming principle exists to kill. If there is a closed core vocabulary, it has to be authored now, before the first device publishes one. This is the same shape as a-pane-declares-its-view's closed kind vocabulary, and the two should be answered together or deliberately apart.
